clue.text: Put out broadcast developed with no old characters

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the remaining letters are strewn into a new order
with no says the letters of the following word must be taken away from the fodder first

parts.note: the three letters of old are what get struck out of developed

explanation.surface: A grumble that something was aired after being developed without its old features.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike O, L and D from DEVELOPED to leave D, E, V, E, P, E, and 'broadcast' scatters those six letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is to be annoyed or irritated, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Make couples broadcast despatch under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer, the pieces that come under another are written below it, so they follow it

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to air a programme is to broadcast it
to despatch someone, or bump them off, is to kill; off here is that sense

explanation.surface: Instructions to send something out urgently while making couples.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under pressure' puts AIR and OFF below P.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair off is to form pairs or couples, an idiom with the same meaning.

clue.text: Heartless attitude evident in former partner's revelations

indicators.note: evident in says the trimmed attitude appears inside the former partner's letters

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, and the 's adds S

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is cut out

parts.note: a posture is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: A cold manner shows through in an ex's disclosures.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'partner's' supplies the final S, so the trimmed attitude sits between the two parts of that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposures are disclosures of hidden facts, so revelations is a synonym.

clue.text: Objective solution for disorder's not about to last

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective

indicators.note: not here tells you the word for about is missing from the cure

parts.note: a cure is the answer to an illness or disorder
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A goal of fixing a disorder is said to fall short of lasting.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'about' is circa, the Latin used before uncertain dates.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on or survive, which is what endure means as a verb.

clue.text: Army limit a railway having one interchange

indicators.note: having one interchange means a single swap of two letters' places in limit, which reorders that word

explanation.surface: Railway jargon: an army line with one junction where trains change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interchange' sounds like a railway junction, but one swap of L and M in 'limit' gives MILIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The military means the armed forces collectively, especially the army.

clue.text: Satirist reveals something the viewer wants to see

definitions.text: something the viewer wants to see

indicators.note: reveals says the answer is exposed among the letters of satirist

explanation.surface: A satirist shows the audience what it is eager to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' sounds like an audience member, but it is anyone with eyes, and the eye needs this part to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye controls the light entering it, so anyone looking needs one to see.

clue.text: Training run tired unauthorised entrant

indicators.note: training something reshapes it, as a gardener trains a vine, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted runner in training is turned away as a gatecrasher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' reads as part of the jog, but it is the anagram signal for RUN TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is someone who enters a place without permission.

clue.text: Biting cold found in very dry surroundings

indicators.note: found in says the cold letter sits inside the next piece
surroundings says the very dry word forms the outside around the cold letter

parts.note: arid means extremely dry, like a desert
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A sharp chill met in a parched desert landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid smoke or a remark bites, stinging the senses or feelings sharply.

clue.text: Felt desire nobody on the far right merited

indicators.note: the far right of a word is its last letter

parts.note: earned means deserved or merited

explanation.surface: No one on the political far right deserved to want anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the far right' sounds political, but it just picks Y, the end of 'nobody'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearned means longed or wished for, i.e. felt desire, in the past tense.

clue.text: Stop: I'm getting deep in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so the letters of deep are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cry for help: halt, I am sinking into serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after 'Stop' marks off the definition; the rest reads as a sentence but is all wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to hinder or block progress, a synonym of stop as a verb.

clue.text: Men on International Court entering through station

indicators.note: entering says the court and the men go inside the word for through

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: ICT stands for International Criminal Tribunal or Court
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers at an international tribunal passing through a railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the usual crossword shorthand for soldiers; VICTORIA is a major London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a well-known London railway terminus, so it is an example of a station.

clue.text: School promoted unchanged plans

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, so in a down answer the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: same means unchanged

explanation.surface: A school went up a division with its strategies left as they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns SAME upwards into EMAS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemas are outlines or models, a more technical word for plans.

clue.text: Check unusually robust conclusions of scientific experiment

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unusual way, so these letters are shuffled
conclusions of takes the final letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Verify the surprisingly strong results of a lab trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges ROBUST into OBSTRU; the endings of 'scientific' and 'experiment' add C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to hold back or block, which is what obstruct means.

clue.text: Tax banned rubbish bags retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking backwards, so the concealed letters read from right to left
bags means holds inside, so the answer is concealed within the next words

explanation.surface: A levy on prohibited refuse sacks applied to past years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' and 'retrospectively' together find NNEDRUB backwards across 'banned rubbish'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to strain or load them heavily, the verb sense of burden.

clue.text: Returns from place of religious instruction?

indicators.note: a place of religious instruction is read with that subject placed before the place

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
a venue is a place where events are held

explanation.surface: Asks what comes back from a centre for teaching faith.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is British school shorthand for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, such as the sums brought in as returns on investment.

clue.text: Drive off shortly after reversing car

indicators.note: after reversing says the street and the cut-down word are read backwards together

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street names

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, before shortening

explanation.surface: A motorist's instruction to pull away once the car has backed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts OFF to OF; DR + OF then reads backwards. The Ford Model T and others make this a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford is a car maker, and a car is often named by its make.

clue.text: Alluded to Red Guards fight over head of state

indicators.note: guards means surrounds and protects, so red goes round the rest

parts.note: taken as written, RED split around the rest

indicators.note: over means covering, so the fight word lies over and around the ruler

parts.note: to fence is to fight with swords
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: Chinese Red Guards fighting over who leads the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Guards' looks like Mao's militia, but 'Guards' is a container signal; ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To have referenced something is to have mentioned or cited it, so alluded to fits.

clue.text: Sweetener in 60% of corruption cases succeeded in New York

indicators.note: cases means encloses, as a case holds something
sixty percent of a ten-letter word is its first six letters
in puts the succeeded letter inside New York

parts.note: S is short for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A sweetener features in most corruption trials won in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruption' has ten letters, so sixty percent is exactly its first six.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn syrup is a sugary liquid made from maize starch and used to sweeten food.

clue.text: One confined by banks depressed about reversal of policy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sad word goes round the turned policy

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed

indicators.note: reversal of says the letters of the policy word run backwards

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A sad figure laments a policy U-turn by the banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance but means riverbanks, and 'depressed' is a mood, not a slump.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs between its two banks, and this one rises in Ethiopia to join the White Nile.

clue.text: Not happy with complaint covering limitations of poll

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the ailing word goes around the poll's edges

parts.note: having a complaint, i.e. an illness, is being diseased

indicators.note: limitations are limits, the outside letters of the word poll

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about the limited scope of an opinion survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitations of' takes P and L from 'poll'; 'covering' puts them inside DISEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Displeased means annoyed or dissatisfied, a synonym of being unhappy.

clue.text: Express opposition to dictator's decline

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating a letter, so the word is as it is spoken out loud

parts.note: a descent is a fall or decline

explanation.surface: Objecting to a tyrant's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' is not a tyrant but someone dictating, whose spoken 'descent' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to disagree publicly, voicing opposition.

clue.text: What provides some personal support for chief?

definitions.meaning: the curved part of the foot that bears the body's weight
principal or leading, as in an archenemy

explanation.surface: A riddle about what props a person up as a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot's arch supports weight, and arch as an adjective means chief or principal.

clue.text: Yorkshire making regular deductions arranged cover for members

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
regular deductions take out letters at even intervals, here the fourth and eighth of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire firm docking pay regularly to fund members' cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making regular deductions' drops K and R, the 4th and 8th letters, to leave YOSHIRE; 'arranged' reorders it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery is stockings and socks, which cover the legs; limbs are members.

clue.text: Anger about record being overturned is marked

indicators.note: about means around, so the noticed word surrounds the flipped record

parts.note: seen means noticed or marked

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the record reads upwards

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Rage over a record being overturned is marked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' is a vinyl disc here, not a legal ruling, despite 'overturned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means bad temper or spite, once thought to come from that organ.

clue.text: Gloomy star conveying lines with little energy

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the star holds the lines and energy

parts.note: the sun is a star
L is short for line; LL is lines
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A moody star delivers her lines with no energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' sounds like an actor, but it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullen means sulky and morose, close to gloomy.

clue.text: Inhuman South American priest's reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is as it sounds

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A cruel South American cleric is the subject of reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inhuman' suggests cruelty, but just means not a person: an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is an Andean animal, so it is a South American that is not human.

clue.text: Uses right attitude to intervene in medical matter

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so these letters go inside the medical matter

parts.note: pus is matter from an infected wound
a pose is a posture or attitude

explanation.surface: The right attitude when stepping into a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Purposes are aims or functions, so they are the uses something is put to.

clue.text: All-points bulletin?

parts.note: a police alert to every unit is read as a broadcast covering every compass point

explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a report of current events, and the four compass point letters spell it.

clue.text: Tested material cut in a revolutionary manner

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the fabric and the chop read backwards

parts.note: denim is a cotton material
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Fabric slashed by radicals was put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests rebels, but only signals turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: To be examined is to be inspected or tested.

clue.text: Doggerel essentially ruined Eliot's name

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so those letters are jumbled
essentially means at its core, so only the inner letters of doggerel are used

explanation.surface: Bad verse spoiled the novelist's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes OGGERE, all but the ends; 'ruined' reorders it.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of novelist Mary Ann Evans, so it is her first name.

clue.text: Go through part of song by triphop's premier artist

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of triphop is taken

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a verse is a section of a song

explanation.surface: A lyric section on a trip-hop record by the leading performer.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross or pass over, so go through is a synonym.

clue.text: Fashionable photograph verges on parody

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph

indicators.note: verges are edges, so the first and last letters of parody

explanation.surface: A trendy photo that comes close to being a spoof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verges on' looks like 'almost', but picks P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means stylish or smart, as in a snappy dresser.
